# Q/C Technologies Reports Over $10 Million in Cash and Investments to Fund Development of Its Optical Processing Unit


November 16, 2026 9:15am EST[Download as PDF](https://d1io3yog0oux5.cloudfront.net/_c70122e283bd4692a72250e5b73a3b45/mymd/news/2026-11-16_Q_C_Technologies_Reports_Over_10_Million_in_Cash_92.pdf)


*Company is developing an optical processing unit (OPU) designed to accelerate core AI computations using light, targeting energy constraints facing AI infrastructure*


*CTO Yossi (Yossef) Ehrlichman, Ph.D., brings expertise in integrated photonics, electro-optic devices and architectures for optical computing*


*Initial device designs on the Company's optical computing roadmap expected to be unveiled before year-end 2026, with a hardware demonstration planned for 2027*


SAN FRANCISCO, Nov. 16, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Q/C Technologies, Inc. (Nasdaq: QCLS) ("Q/C" or the "Company"), a developer of next-generation optical computing solutions, today reported that it ended the third quarter of 2026 with over $10 million in cash, cash equivalents and marketable securities, a balance sufficient for funding its Optical Processing Unit (OPU) development in progress now through key milestones in 2027 and beyond.


An OPU is a processor designed to perform the core mathematical operations of artificial intelligence with photons rather than electrons. Modern AI is dominated by matrix multiplication. Conventional AI chips use electronic circuits to perform these operations, while computation and data movement consume power and generate heat. In conventional AI systems, moving data between memory and processors adds substantial energy overhead. In an optical processor, the multiplication is performed as light propagates through an engineered medium, with the potential for dramatically lower energy per operation, higher bandwidth and lower latency. Optical computing has been pursued for decades; Q/C believes recent advances in silicon photonics manufacturing and in diffractive neural network research have made it newly practical to build.


Q/C is pursuing two complementary technical paths to its OPU: an integrated silicon-photonic chip (PIC) built on established semiconductor fabrication processes, and a free-space diffractive architecture building on recent academic work demonstrating optical systems performing generative AI tasks. The Company is evaluating these approaches against application requirements, including computational accuracy, energy efficiency, scalability and manufacturability. The Company is also developing the components that move data between electronics and light — historically the main bottleneck that has held optical computing back.


Dr. Ehrlichman leads the Company's technology roadmap. Prior to his appointment as CTO in September 2026, he served as the Company's Founding Manager of PIC Development. His previous roles include Senior Photonics Engineer at Bascom Hunter, Senior Principal Engineer at Raytheon, and Senior Member of Technical Staff at Axalume, as well as postdoctoral research appointments at the University of California San Diego and the University of Colorado Boulder. He is a named inventor on patents and patent applications spanning electro-optic modulation, optical signal generation, and photonic manipulation — technologies relevant to photonic computing and AI acceleration. Much of his career has been spent at the boundary between electronics and photonics, where signals cross from one domain to the other. Since the start of the year, the Company has assembled a team of photonics engineers and is establishing laboratory facilities in San Diego, California.


“For decades, optical computing has been held back not by the optics, but by everything around them: getting data into and out of light without giving back the gains,” said Yossi Ehrlichman, Ph.D., Chief Technology Officer. “That boundary between electronics and photonics is where I’ve spent my career. We’re building the complete system, the optical core and the pieces that connect it to the digital world, and we expect to unveil our initial designs before year-end 2026, followed by a hardware demonstration in 2027.”


The Company's Quarterly Report on Form 10-Q for the period ended September 30, 2026, is available through the SEC's website at[www.sec.gov](https://www.globenewswire.com/Tracker?data=m-_XjZQT8Evq7MJ6LXobw_3cRnX76QnblV0L_DhsrqE0qGecX41qYyDcptDPRTi_R3iQNQ33hmIk5gQSMaq-YA==) .


**About Q/C Technologies, Inc.**


Q/C Technologies is developing optical computing technologies that use light and interference to perform core mathematical operations for AI and other computational workloads. The Company's development efforts span optical processing architectures and supporting devices for data conversion, control and nonlinear operations. Its goal is to improve computational throughput and energy efficiency at the system level. Learn more at[qctechnologies.com](https://www.globenewswire.com/Tracker?data=C0UixHswqPAQyfLa7Kr7Q7IY6uPQLdIy9Occp1-pxvASd4tkZktQRs3LYikKcCCFLPumffCOVsCvwHetkr5ky06n8gFPmHhjpE79uHdspdw=) .
